clue.text: City ace adopts suitable position when international's dropped

parts.note: an ace at something is a master of it
a niche is the place that suits you
I = international, removed from NICHE to leave NCHE

explanation.surface: A star player moves into a better role once the international game is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is left alone at the front, where it reads like Manchester City, the football club, which suits the ace and the international.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is a city in north-west England.

clue.text: Study one of Plato's letters on retired boxer

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A student reads Greek philosophy perched on a boxer who has hung up his gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like the dog, which is also a pug, so either reading lands on the same letters. To mug up is British slang for cramming.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is to study hard in a short time, as before an exam.

clue.text: Someone putting forward candidate's motion ran for Reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A candidate's proposal was put to the vote and carried in favour of Reform, the political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Reform' looks like the name of a party, but a capital letter proves nothing in a crossword; here it is only the instruction to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominator formally proposes a candidate for election or office.

clue.text: That woman's bed contains a second resigned prime minister

parts.note: her = belonging to that woman
a berth is a bed on a ship or train
taken as written
s = second, the unit of time
to resign is to quit

explanation.surface: A woman's bed turns out to hold a prime minister who had recently resigned: a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: HER + BERT(A S QUIT)H. Herbert Asquith was the British Liberal prime minister from 1908 to 1916, and 'resigned' is a sly nod, since he was pushed out mid-war.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith led the British government from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Betrayal of subversive group reportedly revealed

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the clue works by sound

parts.note: a cell is a small secret unit of plotters
once a secret is out, it has been revealed

explanation.surface: A news report: a secret cell has been betrayed and exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half changes spelling: CELL is heard, SELL is written. OUT is spelt as it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-out is a betrayal of one's side or principles.

clue.text: Stirs up old urban areas abandoned by India

parts.note: ex = former, as in ex-wife
cities are urban areas
India is I in the NATO alphabet; one I leaves CITIES to give CITES

explanation.surface: Unrest stirs in decaying towns that India has left behind, as in the end of empire.
explanation.walkthrough: CITIES has two Is; dropping either leaves CITES.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite a crowd is to stir it up.

clue.text: The setter's wife getting very first watch

parts.note: v = very, the standard abbreviation
the setter has = I'VE; its V is the one sent to the front
w = wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The setter's wife gets first look at something.
explanation.walkthrough: I'VE (the setter has) plus W gives IVEW; 'very first' says its V (very) comes first, making VIEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both verbs mean to look at something attentively, as you would a programme.

clue.text: Doctors cutting two twisted feet

indicators.note: the doctors cut into the pair, sitting between its two Is
twisting turns the whole thing round, so it reads backwards

parts.note: II = two in Roman numerals
the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' body

explanation.surface: Surgeons operate on a patient with two twisted feet.
explanation.walkthrough: I(BMA)I, then turned round. Feet here are metrical units in verse: an iamb is a short syllable then a long one, and iambi is its plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi, plural of iambus, are metrical feet.

clue.text: Leave with first-class boor, running to catch the end of Sherlock

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of Sherlock

parts.note: w = with, as in w/
A = first-class, as in A1
a lout is a boor
the last letter of Sherlock
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A detective story: a first-class boor runs off to catch Sherlock at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' reads as the boor dashing off, but it only supplies a short word. 'Leave' is a verb here, not permission to go.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase means abandoning a partner or a commitment, a pointed kind of leaving.

clue.text: Secretive Barking dockland garage

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: An address: a secretive garage in the Barking docklands of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London near the Thames docks, so it reads as a place name; in British slang 'barking' also means mad, which is its job here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloak-and-dagger describes secretive dealings, like those of spies.

clue.text: Roof of school building's entrance on left

indicators.note: the way in to a word is its first letter

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
the first letter of building
on = re = concerning
L = left

explanation.surface: Directions to a school: the roof of the building, entrance on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' wants to be a place with a roof; it is a school of whales, a gam. 'On' reads as a position but is the preposition meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambrel is a roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steeper, as on a barn.

clue.text: Cathartic phone conversation about love and marriage on vacation

parts.note: a call is a conversation by phone
love = nil = O in tennis scores

indicators.note: a word on vacation is vacated, emptied of its middle

parts.note: MarriagE with its middle cleared out

explanation.surface: A heart-to-heart phone call about love and marriage while away on holiday, and a good release.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL(O + ME)L. 'Cathartic' reads as emotional release; it is the medical sense, a purgative.
explanation.definitionFit: Calomel, mercurous chloride, was long used as a purgative, which is what a cathartic is.

clue.text: Shortly key Conservative opens SEND festival

indicators.note: the next word is cut short by its last letter
the pair opens SEND's word up by going into it

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
C = Conservative
to key data is to ENTER it; cut short, ENTE

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician opens a festival for SEND, the British school term for special educational needs and disabilities.
explanation.walkthrough: P(ENTE + C)OST. The capitals on SEND make it look like the British acronym for special educational needs, but it is only the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is the Christian festival seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Friend's current game on live

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'on' puts the first pieces after the next

parts.note: I am = I live, I exist
I is the physics symbol for electric current
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A friend's latest game is on live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry, 'on' means placed after, so the word for 'live' comes first. 'Current' and 'live' both sound electrical, which hides their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used in English too.

clue.text: Small wings on primitive bird

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of PrimitivE
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Small wings found on an ancient bird, like those of an early flier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small wings' reads as one thing, but 'Small' is the definition and the wings belong to 'primitive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit is French for small, used in English in terms like petit four.

clue.text: Delirious partners holding king and joker

indicators.note: a delirious mind is scrambled, so the letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
K = king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A card table: giddy bridge partners hold both the king and the joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King and joker' look like two cards held together; only the king is wordplay, and 'joker' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster is someone who plays jokes on people.

clue.text: Will magazine for teachers tone down coverage of NASUWT?

parts.note: the TES, formerly the Times Educational Supplement, is the British teachers' weekly
to tame is to tone down

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of NASUWT

explanation.surface: Will a teachers' magazine soften its reporting on NASUWT, a British teachers' union?
explanation.walkthrough: The TES is the British weekly for teachers, and the NASUWT is one of their trade unions; only its first and last letters count. 'Will' opens the question but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal synonym: the document disposing of a person's estate, as in the phrase last will and testament.

clue.text: Testing times in the morning at home with topless person outside

indicators.note: the word loses its top, which in a down entry is its first letter
the headless word goes around the others

parts.note: a person is a being; topless, EING
someone at home is in
a.m. = in the morning
x is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: A morning at home facing tough exam times, with someone half-dressed standing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: E(X + AM + IN)ING. 'Testing times' looks like a phrase for hard days, but the definition stops at 'Testing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Examining is testing, as an examiner tests a candidate.

clue.text: Stopping rock star on live being punched by Republican

indicators.note: in an across clue, the first piece comes after the next

parts.note: they are = they live, they exist
R = Republican
Sting is the British rock singer, formerly of the Police

explanation.surface: A rock star performing live is punched by a Republican, and the police stop the show.
explanation.walkthrough: AR(R)E + STING: the clue gives STING on ARE, and 'on' in an across entry puts STING second.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to arrest a process is to halt it, as when a doctor arrests a disease.

clue.text: Reason I won't fire

parts.note: to infer is to reason from evidence
'no' is what you say for 'I won't'

explanation.surface: A soldier refuses the order to fire and gives his reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' reads as a noun, the soldier's excuse; it is the verb, to infer. 'Fire' reads as the order to shoot but is the definition, a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym by degree: the word names a blaze so large and fierce it is out of control.

clue.text: Young lady bored by seeing that primarily ornamental stone

parts.note: a girl is a young lady
as = seeing that, since

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of ornamental

explanation.surface: A young lady is bored stiff at the sight of a stone that is mostly ornamental.
explanation.walkthrough: GIR(AS + O)L. 'Ornamental stone' looks like the definition, but 'ornamental' supplies the O and the definition is just 'stone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol is a fire opal, a gemstone used ornamentally.

clue.text: Some red raw, now fatigued

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

parts.note: reD RAW Now

explanation.surface: Eyes red and raw, a tired face at the end of a long day.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across all three words, taking the last letter of 'red' and the first of 'now'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks tired and strained.

clue.text: Regularly quiz nobleman, mostly about invasive species

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady every-other step
most of the word, all but its last letter
turns the joined pieces round

parts.note: qUiZ, the even letters
DUKE without its last letter

explanation.surface: A quiz host keeps asking a lord about invasive species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' comes last, so it turns both pieces round together, not just the duke. Kudzu is a Japanese vine rather than an animal, so 'species' covers plants too.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudzu is a climbing vine that has spread aggressively across the southern United States.

clue.text: Hang troubled padre

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: A troubled chaplain facing the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang' reads as a grim fate for the priest; it means to drape cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for letting cloth fall loosely in folds, as curtains do.

clue.text: Validate African country's concerning energy reserves

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep back

parts.note: as for = concerning
Mali's, with the S from the possessive
E = energy, as in E = mc²

explanation.surface: Validate an African country's claims about its energy reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR(MALIS)E. 'Energy reserves' looks like a single phrase, oil or gas; it is E, followed by the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: making an arrangement official gives it validity, the British -ise spelling.

clue.text: Literal child who misbehaves after temperature's taken

indicators.note: in the sense of taken off or away, so the temperature's letter is removed

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child
T = temperature, removed from the front

explanation.surface: A literal-minded child playing up once his temperature has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: A literal is printers' slang for a typing mistake; 'Literal' reads as an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal is a misprint, an error of a letter or two.

clue.text: Quietly leaving bread portion on the counter for rat

indicators.note: counter to the reading direction, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread
p = piano, quietly in music
PART without P

explanation.surface: A bakery scene: a slice of bread quietly slipped onto the counter to feed a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' reads as a kitchen counter; it means going against the usual direction, and it turns the bread and the portion round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain slang synonym: someone who rats on their friends is a betrayer.

clue.text: More wet naked cats adopted by sister

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: Sr = sister, as in a nun's title
MOGGIES without its first and last letters; a moggy is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A sister adopts some hairless cats, and they are soaked from the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: S(OGGIE)R. 'Naked cats' looks like the hairless sphynx breed; it strips MOGGIES to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soggier means more soaked, wetter.

clue.text: Revolutionary possibly does grass

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round

parts.note: does are female deer; 'possibly' flags the example

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is suspected of smoking or selling grass, cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as the verb and 'grass' as cannabis, or as informing on someone; 'does' is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass growing in wet places.

clue.text: Flag extremely nasty gore, beginning to retch

indicators.note: a nasty mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: jolly = very, in British informal speech, as in jolly good

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: anagram fodder
the first letter of retch

explanation.surface: A flag of warning at a scene of gore so nasty it makes you start to retch.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'jolly' is an informal intensifier, as in jolly good. The pirates' flag, skull and crossbones, fits the gory picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the pirates' skull-and-crossbones flag.
